office_does: A U.S. Representative writes and votes on federal legislation, controls federal spending through appropriations, oversees the executive branch, and provides constituent services for the district.
race_blurb: Incumbent Adam Smith (D), in the House since 1997 and top Democrat on Armed Services, faces Republican Doug Basler for the sixth time. Smith took 47% and Basler 22% in a primary where two left-flank challengers split much of the remainder.

candidates.summary: Incumbent U.S. Representative since 1997, former state senator and Seattle prosecutor; ranking member and past chair of the House Armed Services Committee.
highlights: Voted against the FY2027 NDAA in July 2026, citing its $1.6 trillion price tag and anti-LGBTQ+ floor amendments [S6][S13]
Voted to block $3.3 billion in Israel military aid while saying he still supports Israel [S7][S14]
Introduced a resolution to tax capital gains the same as wages [S8]
Supports a path to single-payer healthcare and lists protecting abortion rights as a priority [S1][S3]
Endorsed by the Seattle Times, King County Democrats, Gov. Ferguson and the State Labor Council [S4]

taxes.basis: Introduced a resolution to tax capital gains like wages, saying the ultra-wealthy pay too little; no wealth tax.

spending.basis: Platform invests in housing, job training and workforce programs and opposes domestic cuts, while citing the deficit against the defense budget increase.

safety.basis: Bills on the 988 crisis line and behavioral-health crisis care centers point toward services responses.

climate.basis: Lists protecting Puget Sound and voted against overturning EPA approval of California's at-berth emission standards.

experience.basis: In Congress since 1997, Armed Services ranking member and past chair, with enacted bills.

reform.basis: Accepts PAC money ($563,000 from other committees this cycle) and runs on broad party and union endorsements; no structural-reform planks recorded.

immigration.basis: Co-introduced bills to help immigrants enter the health-care workforce.

healthcare.basis: Repeatedly says the system should be restructured toward 'a path to a single-payer plan like Medicare for All.'

social.basis: Protecting abortion rights is a campaign priority; opposes the transgender military ban and objected to anti-LGBTQ+ NDAA amendments; endorsed by HRC PAC and Planned Parenthood.

defense.basis: Mixed: voted against the FY2027 NDAA on cost and to block $3.3B in Israel aid, and backed the Iran War Powers resolution, while stating continued support for Israel and a strong defense.

candidates.summary: Republican advertising and video-production business owner and former King County GOP vice chair, running against Smith for the sixth time.
highlights: Urges yes votes on I-645, IL26-001 and IL26-638 [S5]
Says the Climate Commitment Act raises energy costs while doing little for the environment [S1]
Pro-life but opposes a federal abortion ban and supports IVF and contraception [S5]
Calls his platform an 'opportunity revolution' focused on cutting costs and barriers to building [S1][S5]

taxes.basis: Urges a yes vote on IP26-645 to repeal the state income tax and names taxes among costs squeezing families.

spending.basis: 'Before we subsidize the price, let's attack the cost'; says big-government policies make it harder to build, hire and afford.

safety.basis: Compassion for people in crisis while 'holding people accountable for crime, addiction-fueled disorder.'

climate.basis: Says the Climate Commitment Act drives up energy costs while doing little for the environment; supports 'reliable and affordable energy.'

experience.basis: No elected record, though a longtime party officer and repeat candidate.

social.basis: Pro-life and supports IL26-638, but opposes a federal abortion ban and supports IVF and contraception.
